fields.meta_description: Take a free workplace safety quiz, then build your own for new hires and toolbox talks, with retakes, supervisor alerts, and your own data.
fields.h1: Build a Safety Quiz From Your Own Site Rules
fields.hero_description: Take the safety quiz below, or build one from your site rules with a pass mark and every answer saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Goes Into Your Safety Quiz
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the questions, the scoring, and the table behind each attempt from one prompt. Another prompt changes any of them.
fields.feature_1:
Questions written from your site rules

Paste your site rules or the outline of a toolbox talk. Emergent writes multiple-choice questions with the right answer marked, and changes any question you flag by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
A pass mark, then a retake

Set the score a worker needs, such as 8 out of 10. Anyone below it sees the questions they missed and the right answers, then takes the quiz again before starting work.
fields.feature_3:
The supervisor hears about a fail

When a worker scores under the pass mark, the app emails their supervisor the name, the score, and each missed question. Send the same alert to a Slack channel if you prefer.
fields.feature_4:
Every attempt in a database you own

Each attempt is a row in a database you own, with the worker, the date, the score, and every answer. Sort by question to find the rule a whole crew keeps getting wrong.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen, on any phone

Workers answer one question per screen on a phone, at the gate or in the break room. Emergent puts no cap on responses, so a crew of 12 and a plant of 400 use one build.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, your code

Host the quiz on your own domain, included in Emergent and billed in credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep it with your training files.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Workplaces Run Their Safety Quiz
fields.tab_content_1:
5 new hires retake it before day two

On day one, each new hire at Coldbrook Mill Distribution takes a 10-question safety quiz. The pass mark is 8, and 26 of 31 March hires passed first time. Supervisor Ondrej Salo got the missed questions for the other 5 by email, went over those rules with each, and all 5 passed the retake before day two.
fields.tab_content_2:
With 9 workers unsure, the fall talk runs twice

Every Monday at 7:00, a Halloran Sands Builders crew hears a toolbox talk and answers 5 questions on their phones. After the fall protection talk, 9 of 22 workers missed the question on when fall protection starts. Foreman Matthias Groult got the count in a Slack message and gave the talk again on Tuesday.
fields.tab_content_3:
Synthesis averages 5.9 and rereads its own sheets

Once a year, Quarrow Bioscience sends its 64 lab staff an 8-question refresher on chemical labels and safety data sheets, with scores split by lab group. Three groups averaged 7.0 or higher out of 8. Synthesis averaged 5.9. The safety officer booked that group an hour on the sheets for its most-used solvents.
fields.tab_content_4:
Where 58 staff went wrong after a fire drill

The week after its fire drill, Linnet Row Kitchens sends 6 questions on extinguishers and exits to the 140 staff at its 3 restaurants. Of those, 58 chose the front lot as the assembly point, though it moved to the back lot in May. Each general manager posted a map of the new assembly point by the back door.

quiz.title: Workplace Safety Quiz: How Well Do You Know the Basics?
quiz.intro: Eight questions on falls, noise, fire, color codes, and chemicals, each answer drawn from OSHA. Your site's own rules and training come first.

questions.text: In general industry workplaces, at what height does OSHA require fall protection?
questions.explanation: Four feet is the general industry height. Other industries use a different one, so check the height for your own work.

source.quote: OSHA requires that fall protection be provided at elevations of four feet in general industry workplaces

questions.text: On a construction site, at what height does OSHA require fall protection?
questions.explanation: Construction is six feet. Five feet applies in shipyards and eight feet in longshoring.

source.quote: five feet in shipyards, six feet in the construction industry and eight feet in longshoring operations

questions.text: At what noise level must a general industry employer run a hearing conservation program?
questions.explanation: The level is 85 decibels averaged over an 8-hour shift, not a single loud moment.

source.quote: when employee noise exposures equal or exceed 85 decibels (dBA) as an 8-hour time-weighted average

questions.text: You have to raise your voice to talk to a coworker how close to you before noise may be over 85 decibels?
questions.explanation: Treat this as a quick check on the floor, then ask for a measured reading if you are unsure.

source.quote: If you need to raise your voice to speak to someone 3 feet away, noise levels might be over 85 decibels

questions.text: Which color does OSHA name as the basic color for danger signs and emergency stop buttons?
questions.explanation: Learn where the red stop button sits on every machine you run, before you need it.

source.quote: Red shall be the basic color for the identification of

questions.text: Using a portable fire extinguisher, where do you point the nozzle?

options.text: At the top of the flames
At the base of the fire

questions.explanation: Pull the pin, aim low, and keep a clear way out behind you while you use it.

source.quote: Aim low, pointing the extinguisher nozzle (or its horn or hose) at the base of the fire.

questions.text: Your extinguisher is empty and the fire is still burning. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Plan your way out before you approach a fire, and never let it come between you and the exit.

source.quote: Evacuate immediately if the extinguisher is empty and the fire is not out.

questions.text: How many sections does a safety data sheet for a hazardous chemical have?
questions.explanation: Find the sheet for each chemical you handle, and read its first-aid section before you need it.

source.quote: Safety Data Sheets: Will now have a specified 16-section format.

results.title: Time to Review the Basics
results.description: You scored 4 or fewer. Read the explanation under each question you missed, then ask your supervisor where your site keeps its rules on falls, noise, and fire. A quiz checks what you remember, not how you work.

results.title: Solid on the Basics
results.description: You scored 5 or 6. You know the core rules, with a gap or two. Look at the questions you missed and check how your own site handles each one, since site rules can go further than these.

results.title: Sharp on the Rules
results.description: You scored 7 or 8 and know these OSHA basics well. A quiz score is what you remember on the day. Keep following your site's training, and ask before any task that is new to you.

quiz_plan.promise: the quiz plays the page's promise: a safety quiz a visitor can take, whose results answer what the H1 says it builds

plan.angle: The top 10 is static question lists from sign vendors and trainers (MySafetySign, OSHA.net, SmartSign, Red Hat Safety) plus one ProProfs quiz. This page lets a visitor play a sourced workplace safety quiz right here, then shows four workplaces running quizzes built from their own site rules: a new-hire quiz with a pass mark and retake, a toolbox talk quiz on phones, a hazard communication refresher scored by lab group, and a quiz after a fire drill. Every attempt lands in a database the company owns, and the FAQ gives question-writing and scoring advice the lists skip, with no claim that a quiz proves anyone works safely.
tab_stories: Coldbrook Mill Distribution gives each new hire a 10-question safety quiz on day one with a pass mark of 8; in March 26 of 31 passed first time, and supervisor Ondrej Salo got an email listing the missed questions for the 5 who retook it.

After the Monday toolbox talk on fall protection, 22 workers at a Halloran Sands Builders site answer 5 questions on their phones; 9 of 22 missed the question on when a harness is needed, so foreman Matthias Groult covered it again at the scaffold on Tuesday.

Quarrow Bioscience runs an 8-question refresher on labels and safety data sheets for 64 staff in 4 lab groups; the dashboard shows Synthesis averaging 5.9 of 8 against 7.0 or more elsewhere, and that group gets a session on reading the sheets for its own solvents.

After a fire drill at its 3 restaurants, Linnet Row Kitchens sends 140 staff a 6-question quiz on extinguishers and exits; 58 of 140 picked the wrong assembly point, and each manager posted a map by the back door.
